subject: Access snapshot & query-replay request for compliance review
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Access snapshot & query-replay request for compliance review

Hi Rajiv / Acme Security team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so your compliance team has everything in one place.

Call highlights:
- Scope: verification of who accessed what/when for Redwood-hosted inference calls tied to Acme workloads (last 90 days).
- Deliverables requested: an "access snapshot" (chronological lines) and a separate "query-replay" package if feasible for auditing specific request flows.
- Residency / retention clarifications: Acme asked for confirmation that logs can be produced and retained in US regions only, and whether token-level PII is ever present in stored logs.

Action items we agreed:
1) Acme to confirm exact retention window you want (default ask: 90 days).
2) Redwood to deliver an access snapshot CSV template and an example sample output.
3) If needed, Redwood will package a query-replay bundle (request IDs, request bodies redacted as agreed) — delivery ETA TBD after internal sign-off.

To make work easier for your auditors, we plan to include the following columns in the snapshot: timestamp (ISO 8601), user_email (or hashed id), action (API call / UI access), resource (model, project id), ip_address, session_id, request_id, redaction_flag, residency_region. If you prefer different fields, tell us and we'll adjust.

Attached: access_snapshot_template.csv (blank template) and a draft MOP (method-of-processing) for Acme to sign off. We can produce two formats: CSV (flat) and NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — which format does your tools prefer?

Next steps / timeline:
- If you confirm 90 days and CSV preferred, we can provide the CSV sample within 3 business days after we receive signed MOP.
- Query-replay package (if requested) will require a short feasibility check from Product/Security; estimate 5-7 business days after go-ahead.

Please reply with: confirmation of retention window, preferred format (CSV or NDJSON), and whether you require hashed identifiers or full emails in the snapshot. Also confirm the contact for signature on the MOP (legal or security).

Thanks,

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: access_snapshot_template.csv, redwood-signed-mop.pdf

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access snapshot & query-replay request for compliance review

Vivek — thanks for the recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we sign anything:

1) Retention window: 90 days is fine for the initial snapshot. We may later request a 365-day pull for eDiscovery, but let's start with 90.
2) Fields: we want timezone-normalized timestamps (UTC preferred) and a monotonically increasing sequence number per row to make tamper-evident comparisons.
3) PII & prompts: do your stored logs ever include raw prompt text or token-level PII? If yes, can those be redacted in the snapshot but included in the replay bundle under a secure, ephemeral transfer?
4) KV cache and ephemeral artifacts: if a request hits a KV cache, will the snapshot indicate that as a flag and include an aggregate count? We need to understand whether replaying will reconstruct those cache hits.

Also, our legal team needs to review the MOP. Who should our signer send the signed MOP to?

If you can address (2) and (3) in your first sample it would make the review much faster.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Lead InfoSec, Acme Health
rajiv@acmehealth.com
security@acmehealth.com

Quick priorities for Product/Security:
- Can we produce UTC timestamps and a sequence number? (I assume yes but need confirmation.)

Acme needs the initial snapshot by Oct 19 to keep their audit window. Please advise ETA and any blockers so I can update Rajiv.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Access snapshot & query-replay request for compliance review

Vivek —

We can handle this. Summary of what Security/Product can deliver and constraints:

Deliverables (what we'll provide):
- Access snapshot (CSV + NDJSON sample): UTC timestamp, sequence_number, user_email (optionally hashed), action, resource, ip_address, session_id, request_id, cache_flag, cache_hit_count, residency_region, redaction_flag.
- Replay package: for a limited set of request_ids we can provide request metadata and redacted request bodies. We cannot run an exact stateful replay that rehydrates ephemeral KV caches; instead we will include cache_hit_count and a flag indicating a cache-dependent response.
- Sample CSV: snapshot-sample-20261014.csv (attached) with fake/anonymized rows for format verification.

PII handling / prompts:
- Logs do not retain token-level PII in the clear in long-term cold storage by default. Prompt text can be present in short-lived logs and in the request payloads retained for a configurable retention window. For the snapshot we will apply the following: full prompt text will be redacted (replaced with "[REDACTED]") unless Acme explicitly requests an encrypted replay bundle. The replay bundle will store request bodies encrypted at rest, delivered over a secure transfer (SFTP or signed one-time download link) and require a signed MOP + BAA if PHI is possible.

Regional residency:
- We can produce the export containing only US-region metadata. If you require the raw replay bundle to be stored in a US-only location, we can stage it in our us-east-1 data plane and deliver via a US-based transfer.

ETA:
- CSV sample (attached) and template: 1 business day (we are attaching sample now).
- Full 90-day CSV export: 3 business days after signed MOP/confirmation of hashed vs raw emails.
- Replay package feasibility + delivery plan: 5–7 business days after final scoping and signed MOP.

Next steps for Acme:
1) Confirm hashed vs full emails in snapshot. If hashed, specify hash algorithm or accept our salted SHA-256.
2) Sign MOP and, if applicable, initiate BAA process (we will loop Legal).
3) Confirm preferred transfer method for any encrypted replay bundle (SFTP or signed link).

I've attached snapshot-sample-20261014.csv for format review and a short readme. Ben, Marissa — please confirm there are no product blockers to pulling sequence numbers over the requested window.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: snapshot-sample-20261014.csv

Neha/Vivek — this looks good, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few confirmations from Acme: 

- We accept UTC timestamps and the sequence_number column.
- Please use salted SHA-256 hashing for user identifiers in the snapshot; Acme will retain a separate mapping in our own key store for linkage.
- We will sign the MOP and route it to vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com; legal may request a formal BAA — please have your legal team contact legal@acmehealth.com to kick that off.
- For the replay bundle, SFTP to an Acme-controlled endpoint is preferred.

Once we receive the CSV sample we will do a quick schema check and confirm. Appreciate the clear constraints on cache replay — that matches our expectations.

—Rajiv
Lead InfoSec, Acme Health
